introduction-its-not-just-a-virtual-mach.core: Modern EC2 instances run on the Nitro System, which offloads networking, storage and management from the host CPU onto dedicated hardware cards, with a minimal hypervisor. Nearly all the host's CPU and memory go to your instance, performance is close to bare metal, and isolation is enforced in hardware.

first_principles.problem: Traditional hypervisors steal CPU cycles for I/O and management, causing jitter and lower performance.
truths: Software virtualisation of I/O costs host CPU.
Dedicated hardware can do it faster.
A smaller hypervisor means a smaller attack surface.
derivation: **Offload** VPC networking and EBS to Nitro cards.
Use a **security chip** for hardware root of trust.
Enable **bare-metal** instances with the same model.

analogy.title: A restaurant chef with a dedicated support team
analogy.story: Dishwashers, runners and buyers handle everything else, so the chef only cooks.
analogy.breaks: Kitchen staff can be reassigned; Nitro functions are fixed in hardware.

example.title: Old vs Nitro host
flow: Xen-era host: ~10–30% CPU to virtualisation and I/O
Nitro: nearly all cores to guests

check.q: What does Nitro offload from the host CPU?
check.a: Networking, storage (EBS) and management functions, onto dedicated Nitro cards.

the-three-pillars-of-nitro.core: Nitro has three parts. Nitro Cards (VPC networking with ENA, EBS NVMe, instance storage and management) do the I/O work. The Nitro Security Chip provides a hardware root of trust that verifies firmware. The Nitro Hypervisor is a stripped-down KVM-based layer that only allocates CPU and memory.

first_principles.problem: Engineers can't explain why Nitro instances show EBS volumes as NVMe or why AWS operators can't access instance memory.
truths: Each function benefits from dedicated hardware.
derivation: **Cards**: ENA networking, NVMe EBS, local NVMe, controller.

analogy.title: A secure office building
analogy.story: Mailroom and couriers (cards), tamper-proof foundations (security chip) and a minimal receptionist (hypervisor).
analogy.breaks: Office staff can be bribed; Nitro has no human access path by design.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Use NVMe device names and udev links in fstab, not /dev/xvdf.

code.text:
lsblk
# nvme0n1  8G   root EBS volume (exposed as NVMe by Nitro card)
# nvme1n1  100G data EBS volume

check.q: Why do EBS volumes appear as NVMe devices on Nitro instances?
check.a: The Nitro card presents EBS to the guest through an NVMe interface.

decoding-instance-families-c-m-r-t.core: Instance names encode purpose: family letter (C compute, M general, R memory, T burstable, I storage, P/G accelerators, X large memory), generation number, attributes (g Graviton, a AMD, i Intel, d local NVMe, n network-enhanced) and size. Match the vCPU:memory ratio and features to the workload.

first_principles.problem: A memory-hungry cache runs on compute-optimised instances and swaps.
truths: Newer generations are faster and often cheaper.
Graviton offers better price-performance for compatible code.

analogy.title: Choosing a vehicle by job
analogy.story: Sports car (C), family car (M), lorry (R), moped for short trips (T).
analogy.breaks: Vehicles are bought; instances can be swapped in minutes, so right-size continuously.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: You can predict specs from the name.

check.q: What is the risk with T-family instances under sustained load?
check.a: They run out of CPU credits and get throttled to baseline (or incur charges in unlimited mode).

placement-groups-controlling-physical-lo.core: Placement groups influence where instances land physically. Cluster packs instances close in one AZ for low-latency, high-bandwidth HPC. Spread puts each instance on distinct hardware (max 7 per AZ) for critical small fleets. Partition divides a fleet into racks-like partitions for large distributed systems like Kafka, HDFS and Cassandra.

first_principles.problem: A tightly coupled MPI job is slow because nodes are scattered across racks.
derivation: **Spread**: few critical instances on separate hardware.
**Partition**: large replicated systems; expose partition to the app.

analogy.title: Seating at an event
analogy.story: Team members together at one table (cluster), VIPs at separate tables (spread), or sections for each department (partition).
analogy.breaks: Event seating is visible; AWS hides exact hardware, exposing only partition numbers.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Up to 200 Gbps between nodes with low latency.

code.text:
aws ec2 create-placement-group --group-name mpi --strategy cluster
aws ec2 run-instances --placement GroupName=mpi --instance-type c7gn.16xlarge --count 16 ...

check.q: Which placement strategy suits a 3-node critical database?
check.a: Spread, so each node is on distinct hardware.

spot-instances-and-allocation-strategies.core: Spot instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off, but can be reclaimed with a 2-minute warning. Diversify across instance types and AZs, and use price-capacity-optimized allocation to pick the pools least likely to be interrupted. Design workloads to handle interruption (stateless, checkpointed, queue-driven).

first_principles.problem: A batch fleet on one Spot instance type gets interrupted repeatedly when that pool runs dry.
truths: Each instance type per AZ is a separate capacity pool.
Interruptions are more likely in tight pools.
2 minutes is enough to drain or checkpoint.

analogy.title: Standby airline tickets
analogy.story: Much cheaper, but you might be bumped, so be flexible about flights.
analogy.breaks: Bumped passengers wait; Spot gives a 2-minute warning to save work.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Large savings with rare, handled interruptions.

check.q: Why diversify instance types for Spot?
check.a: Each type/AZ is a separate pool; spreading across many reduces the chance that all capacity is reclaimed at once.
